answer.text: Long one stock, short a correlated 'pair' stock, profiting from relative mispricing

explanation.text: The Logic: Pairs trading is a market-neutral, mean-reversion strategy where the manager identifies two historically correlated securities and simultaneously takes a long position in the relatively under-priced one and a short position in the relatively over-priced one. The bet is on the spread between the pair narrowing back to its historical relationship, not on overall market direction — so the strategy aims for near-zero net beta. Buying only one stock has no offsetting short, while IPO investing and ETF-only strategies are entirely different return drivers. The Trap: Single-stock long, IPO investing, and ETF-only allocations are all directional or category-specific approaches; none captures the long/short, pair-relative-mispricing mechanic that defines pairs trading. Note: The specific "pairs trading" label and the correlated-pair / mean-reversion framing are not used in the NISM Series XIX-B AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook pages checked, which discuss long-short, market-neutral, arbitrage and event-driven strategies in general terms; the framing above reflects general industry strategy terminology rather than a workbook citation.
